LESSON: LANGUAGE USE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.9: Language Use

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Language Use. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you improve your speaking skill?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise objects from an oral text
2. describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension
3. appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LANGUAGE USE
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Language Use helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LANGUAGE USE
Study Language Use like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Recognise objects from an oral text

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise objects from an oral text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise objects from an oral text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Language Use”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise objects from an oral text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Language Use to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Language Use is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Language Use”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise objects from an oral text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Language Use to a partner. (skill: describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Language Use to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise objects from an oral text.
3. Practise this skill: describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate speaking skills to convey information accurately.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Language Use from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Language Use: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Language Use?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you improve your speaking skill?
2. Why does the position of objects affect their description?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Language Use means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise objects from an oral text.
5. Be able to: describe positions of objects in relation to others for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
